task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: The world's hottest cities and countries cluster in the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia. Ar Riyadh (Saudi Arabien) leads cities by average temperature at 45.0°C, followed by Kuwait at 44.4°C. Note: the raw data contains transliteration variants—"Saudi Arabien" and "Saudi Arabia" appear as separate entries. For peak readings, Suva, Fiji recorded an extreme 79.3°C—likely a data anomaly rather than a genuine heatwave, as typical highs there are far lower. Kuwait City (49.2°C) and Baghdad (49.1°C) show more realistic peaks. By country, Saudi Arabien dominates average rankings at 45.0°C, while Fiji Islands tops maximum temperatures at 79.3°C. The data reveals clear geographic clustering: arid desert regions sustain consistently high averages, while tropical locations show extreme but isolated spikes.

report_history.content: The world's hottest cities and countries cluster in the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia. Ar Riyadh, Saudi Arabia leads cities by average temperature at 45.0°C, followed by Kuwait at 44.4°C. For peak readings, Suva, Fiji recorded an extreme 79.3°C—likely a data anomaly rather than a genuine heatwave, as typical highs there are far lower. Kuwait City (49.2°C) and Baghdad (49.1°C) show more realistic peak temperatures. By country, Saudi Arabia dominates average rankings at 45.0°C, while Fiji Islands tops maximum temperatures at 79.3°C. The data reveals clear geographic clustering: arid desert regions sustain consistently high averages, while tropical locations show extreme but isolated spikes. Notable patterns suggest data quality issues warrant caution when interpreting outliers.
